Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report describes a memory leak caused by the use of ThreadLocals in the class org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle. The root cause appears to be that ToStringStyle maintains a static ThreadLocal named REGISTRY of type ThreadLocal<WeakHashMap<Object,Object>>, which is used to hold some form of registry or cache. The method getRegistry() returns the map from this ThreadLocal if present, or an empty map otherwise. However, there is no method provided in ToStringStyle to remove or clear the thread-local map once it is no longer needed, which means that the ThreadLocal and its content can persist even after the thread (e.g., in a web container environment) is done using it. This situation creates a reference chain that prevents garbage collection of classes loaded by a web application, thus triggering a memory leak upon web application reloads.

The failing test testReflectionHierarchy() indirectly triggers the loading and usage of ToStringStyle, leading to the problematic registration and persistence of thread-local data. The absence of a public API method to clear or remove the ThreadLocal from ToStringStyle is the cause of the leak. This diagnosis is consistent with the reported error that mentions the registry is created but never removed and no API exists to remove it, which is essential in container environments where classes need to be garbage collected properly.

The main contributing cause is the static ThreadLocal REGISTRY in ToStringStyle that stays around indefinitely. This highlights the need for addition of methods to clear or remove the registry and for client code (like builders) to call these methods to prevent leaks.

Next, it will be useful to examine if other related classes like HashCodeBuilder also hold similar references and if utility or builder classes correctly clear these thread-local registries after use. It may also help to check for any existing but non-public methods to clear the registry.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
